catalog_entry.label: Longest/shortest play, touchdown and field-goal extremes
contract_types: Player longest reception in a game (over strike)
catalog_entry.target: Probability that the maximum (or minimum) play length of a type over a window (regular season, one game, or one player's receptions in one game) exceeds, falls below or lands in a yardage band.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Extremes of play length are order statistics of a count of eligible plays. Season contracts thin a large count of opportunities (own-1 snaps or, under a return-inclusive reading, long turnover returns for a 99-yard play; end-of-half 65+ yard attempts for a 70+ field goal) through a tail conversion, with the running maximum to date as an absorbing state. Single-game TD-length buckets are the max or min over a random number of touchdowns (zero TDs resolves NO) whose length depends on route (goal-line run, explosive pass, return). The player longest-reception contract is the max over a random number of catches, with a fair-price settlement when the player is active but takes no live snap.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected 70+ makes equal attempts times make probability, so a strong-legged kicker on a coach who never attempts contributes almost nothing.

Altitude plus a strong tailwind adds several effective yards, converting a 66-yard ceiling kicker into a 70-yard threat only in that combined outdoor regime; domes remove wind but give no altitude help.
The 99-yard play probability is the product of the rare exposure count and a tiny conversion, so a rate uncertainty compounds multiplicatively.
More touchdowns raise P(max >= 51) and push the minimum toward 1-2 yards, so the TD count shifts both buckets in opposite directions.

contract.settlement_definition: Five live series, all with sampled rules. KXNFLLONGESTFG (floor 70, greater_or_equal): YES if the longest made field goal of the 2026-27 regular season is 70+ yards. KXNFLLONGESTPLAY (floor 99): YES if any play from scrimmage in the 2026-27 regular season is at least 99 yards on officially recorded Source Agency stats, penalty-nullified plays excluded; whether turnover returns on scrimmage downs count is not stated. KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD are per-game bucket markets (sample: Seattle vs New England, 8 Feb 2026; buckets such as 51+ and 6-10 yards, inclusive bounds) on official play-by-play TD distances; if no touchdown is scored all buckets resolve NO. KXNFLLONGREC (sample strike over 16.5, Buffalo vs Minnesota, 9 Nov 2026): YES if the named player's longest reception in the game exceeds the strike; active but no live play settles at the pre-game fair market price; one live play, even nullified, makes it settle on the recorded longest reception.

rules_evidence.quote: If the longest made field goal is 70+ yards in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settles on the regular-season maximum of made kicks at or above 70 yards; preseason and playoff kicks are outside the window.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a play from scrimmage of at least 99 yards in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A single play from scrimmage of 99+ yards, whole regular season; the text does not say whether interception, fumble or missed-FG returns on scrimmage downs count (see u5).

rules_evidence.quote: therefore plays nullified by penalty are not considered for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: A long play erased by a flag does not count, so penalty-nullification risk reduces the conversion probability.

rules_evidence.quote: If no touchdowns are scored in the game, all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Single-game window; a zero-TD game is a NO for every bucket, so P(no TD) is a point mass the max model must carry.

rules_evidence.quote: Touchdown distances, measured in yards, will be determined based on official play-by-play data from the Source Agencies.
rules_evidence.establishes: TD length comes from official play-by-play; return TDs are not excluded by the text, so the route mix includes returns and zero-yard recoveries.

rules_evidence.quote: All stated yardage ranges are inclusive of both the lower and upper bounds.
rules_evidence.establishes: Shortest-TD buckets such as 6-10 are inclusive at both ends, so integer-yard discreteness matters at 5/6 and 10/11.

rules_evidence.quote: If T.J. Hockenson is active but does not appear in any live play, the market settles to the fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: Active-no-play is not a NO: payoff becomes the pre-game price, so only P(plays) times P(longest > strike | plays) is forecastable.

rules_evidence.quote: Once T.J. Hockenson appears in at least one live play, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on longest reception recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Any live snap, even a nullified one, locks settlement to recorded receptions; a player who plays but has zero catches resolves NO on an over strike.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLLONGESTPLAY is titled 'NFL Longest Touchdown' while the rules say any play from scrimmage of 99+ yards; under the offence-only reading it needs a snap from the own 1, under a return-inclusive reading 99-109 yard interception, fumble or missed-FG returns also qualify (u5).
KXNFLLONGESTFG counts only made kicks; the distance convention and whether a fair-catch free kick (scored as a field goal) is included are not stated (u2).

KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD are single-game bucket ladders with inclusive bounds; a zero-TD game resolves every bucket NO, and zero-yard TDs (fumble recovered in the end zone) can set the minimum. The sample is a Super Bowl; regular-season listings are assumed to share the wording.
KXNFLLONGREC is a per-game player prop with an over-strike (16.5 in the sample); active-but-no-live-play settles at the pre-game fair price, while the inactive case is not described (u6).
Season contracts are regular season only and partly decided at any as-of date by the running maximum to date; one qualifying event ends the market.
contract.settlement_data_source: Officially recorded stats of the Source Agencies (league play-by-play and gamebook); Kalshi names the league as Governing League. Post-game stat corrections are not described in the sampled rules.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Per-game player receiving prop with an active-no-play fair-price clause; its drivers (targets, aDOT, YAC, snap risk) are those of the receiving archetype, not a league-wide extreme. Covered here (stage s7) pending a decision.

mechanism.summary: Three windows share one idea: the outcome is an order statistic over a random count of plays. Season contracts: a 99-yard scrimmage play comes from snaps at the offence's own 1 (punts downed at the 1, goal-line stands, penalties) converted by a full-field breakaway, or, if Kalshi counts turnover returns on scrimmage downs, from 99-109 yard interception, fumble or missed-FG returns; a 70+ yard field goal comes from end-of-half or end-of-game spots where a coach prefers a kick to a Hail Mary, converted by a kicker whose ceiling (record 68 in the 2025 regular season) plus altitude or tailwind reaches 70, in a post-2025 rule era with higher long-kick rates. Running maximum and games left are an absorbing state. Single-game TD buckets are the max or min over the game's touchdowns, with a zero-TD NO mass and route mix (goal-line runs, explosive passes, returns). The player longest-reception contract is the max over a random number of catches, mixed with a fair-price settlement for active-no-play.

stages.name: Opportunity creation: snaps and situations eligible for an extreme
stages.description: The league produces eligible snaps for a 99-yard offensive play through field position (punts downed inside the 2, goal-line stands that turn the ball over at the 1, penalties walking an offence back) and, under a return-inclusive reading, through opponent red-zone and goal-line snaps that can end in a pick or fumble returned the length of the field. For kicks, eligible situations are 0-6 second end-of-half and end-of-game moments within about 68-75 yards of the goal line. Counts are small, clustered in a few team-games and not created by player skill.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts, negative binomial per team-game; heavy clustering in a few games

stages.name: Decision: attempt a long kick or call a deep shot
stages.description: Given an eligible situation the coach chooses a long field goal, Hail Mary, kneel or punt; from the own 1 he chooses safe runs or play-action shots. Coach tendency, the kicker's demonstrated range, timeouts and low-leverage record-chasing (end of first half with the score not at stake, indoors) determine the long-kick attempt; QB deep-ball rate and scheme decide whether a deep shot is called from the 1.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per situation with strong coach heterogeneity; near zero for most coaches

stages.name: Execution tail: breakaway or kick that reaches the threshold
stages.description: A 99-yard play needs an unblocked deep route, a missed deep safety or an untouched run from a compressed field. A 70+ yard make needs ball speed and carry beyond the 68-yard regular-season record, helped by altitude, roof or tailwind, and by the post-2025 kicking-ball preparation rule era. The make curve is a steep logistic tail with very few regular-season points, so preseason long makes and era terms are needed and parameter uncertainty dominates the point estimate.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value tail with parameter uncertainty; orders of magnitude below bulk rates

stages.name: Nullification and aggregation over the remaining schedule
stages.description: A qualifying play or kick survives only if not erased by penalty (offensive holding on a long TD, a kick negated by a roughing flag then re-kicked) and then enters the league-wide maximum. Aggregation takes the running maximum to date, the count of remaining games and rest-of-season availability of kicker and QB, giving a Poisson-thinning probability of at least one qualifying event.
stages.distribution: Poisson-type with rate times remaining games; saturating in games left

stages.name: Settlement and record verification
stages.description: Settlement uses official recorded stats and the exact distance convention for kicks; the longest/shortest-TD buckets still depend on how return and 0-yard recovery TDs are recorded (u1) and the 99-yard play on return inclusion (u5). Stat corrections and source lag can alter the recorded length, and the market resolves from the record at season end.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the record; residual risk from corrections and ambiguity

stages.name: Single-game touchdown count and length mix (longest/shortest TD buckets)
stages.description: For KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD the game produces N touchdowns (both teams, overtime included per official play-by-play), N drawn from each side's drives times TD-per-drive. Each TD length depends on route: goal-line runs and sneaks (1-2 yards), red-zone passes (3-20), explosive scrimmage plays (20-99) and return or recovery TDs (0 to 109). The longest-TD bucket is the max and the shortest-TD bucket the min of these lengths; zero TDs resolves all buckets NO, and more TDs push the max up and the min down at the same time.
stages.distribution: Order statistics of a Poisson-mixture count of TD lengths; point mass at N=0; integer yards with heavy mass at 1-2 and a long right tail

stages.name: Player single-game longest reception (KXNFLLONGREC)
stages.description: The named receiver first must be active and take a live snap (active-no-play settles at the pre-game fair price; inactive handling is unstated). Given he plays, his targets in the game, catch probability per target and the yards of each catch (air yards plus YAC, against the coverage he draws) produce K receptions; the contract settles on the largest. Zero catches is a NO on an over strike, so low-volume tight ends carry a large zero mass, and one busted coverage decides the outcome regardless of total yards.
stages.distribution: Max of K i.i.d.-ish reception lengths with K overdispersed (negative binomial targets times catch rate); zero-catch mass; right-skewed length per catch

nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.label: Own-one-yard-line snap rate (offence backed up at its own 1)
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.mechanism: An offensive scrimmage gain can be at most 99 yards and only from a snap at the offence's own 1-yard line, so the count of such snaps is the exposure for the offensive route to a 99+ yard play.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.rationale: Snaps from the 1 are produced by punts downed or fumbled at the 1, goal-line stands that end in a turnover on downs, and penalties walking the ball back; they are rare, clustered in a few team-games and not stable team traits. The contract is therefore a Poisson-thinning problem whose rate is this count, not any player's long-run yardage.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.measurement: Per team-game, count snaps with yardline_100 = 99 (offence at own 1) from nflverse play-by-play, excluding kneels. Fit a negative-binomial rate on opponent-adjusted punting (inside-10 rate, net punt), defence goal-line stand rate and team penalty profile with 3-season pooling and shrinkage toward the league mean (about 30 team-games of prior weight). Output expected count for each remaining game; as-of = last completed game before the forecast.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.why: Exposure count for the offensive route to a 99+ yard scrimmage play; it bounds YES only under the offence-only reading, since turnover returns on scrimmage downs may also count.

nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.label: Backed-up breakaway conversion (P(99-yard TD | snap from own 1))
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.mechanism: Conditional probability that a snap taken from the own 1 becomes a full-field touchdown, produced by deep-pass completions behind a single-high or man-coverage defence or by an untouched run.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.rationale: The defence is in a compressed field and often in short-yardage or goal-line personnel, which makes a defender-free deep route more plausible on play action, but any penalty (holding, intentional grounding in the end zone) or safety is far likelier than the breakaway. The league sample of true 99-yard plays is a handful in 60 seasons, so the rate must be extrapolated, not counted.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.measurement: Estimate with a hierarchical logistic tail model on all snaps from yardline_100 >= 90 with outcome yards_gained >= 60, then extrapolate to >= 99 with a generalized Pareto tail anchored on the historical 99-yard plays and 80+ yard gains from deep starts; covariates: pass-rush pressure rate, QB deep-ball rate, defence two-high rate, offence tempo; 5-season window, half-life 2 seasons for scheme, shrinkage constant 25 deep-start snaps to the league mean.
free_sources: nflverse participation and FTN charting (free, limited seasons)
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.why: Turns the exposure count into a probability of the one outcome the 99+ yard contract settles on; the tail extrapolation is the main uncertainty.

nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.label: Kicker ceiling range tail (make probability at 66-75 yards)
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.mechanism: Per-kicker make probability beyond the demonstrated range, driven by leg speed, ball strike and launch angle, which pooled accuracy-by-distance tables cannot resolve.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.rationale: Existing long-kick models cover 50+ and 60+ yard attempts; a 70+ make lies beyond the regular-season record (68 yards, 2025, end of first half, indoors; previous record 66). Kickoff depth was a clean leg proxy only before the 2024 dynamic kickoff; since then (touchback to the 35 in 2025) depth is a strategic choice, so it is used only within one rule era and down-weighted, with preseason long makes as direct ceiling evidence.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.measurement: Per kicker, fit a logistic make curve over distance on all regular-season attempts from 45 yards (era fixed effect from nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), with a kicker range term from career max make, 60+ attempt history and preseason makes of 60+ yards (nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence, down-weighted 0.5 per attempt); pre-2024 kickoff distance enters only as a prior for kickers with that history. Shrink toward the position pool with 40 attempts of prior weight; adjust for roof, altitude and wind. Output P(make | attempt at 66, 68, 70, 72 yards, neutral and favourable conditions); as-of = last game before forecast.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.why: The 70+ field goal contract needs a leg-ceiling estimate beyond observed makes; this is the make-probability factor of the expected count of 70+ makes.

nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.label: Long field-goal attempt hazard at end of half and game
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.mechanism: Number of snaps per season where the clock and score make a 65+ yard attempt the best option over a Hail Mary or punt, set by coach choice, timeouts and the kicker's stated range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.rationale: A 70+ attempt almost never occurs in normal play because a punt wins field position; it occurs with 0-5 seconds left in a half or game when only a kick keeps points alive. Whether a coach sends the kicker for 68 or throws a Hail Mary is a policy that varies by coach and by whether the kicker has shown the range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, count snaps with kick_distance >= 60 or qualifying situations (game_seconds_remaining in half <= 6, offence between own 40 and opponent 50, trailing by <= 3 or tied at the half) and estimate P(attempt | situation) by head coach with a hierarchical logit (coach, kicker max make, wind, roof, timeouts, rule era, low-leverage first-half flag for record-chasing). 4-season window; shrink coach rates toward the league with 15 qualifying situations of prior weight. Output expected 65+, 68+, 70+ yard attempts for the remaining schedule.
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play (qtr, game_seconds_remaining, timeout counts, kick_distance)
NFL gamebook text for coach statements (free, scrape)
raw_data: pbp: game_seconds_remaining, half_seconds_remaining, posteam_timeouts_remaining, score_differential, kick_distance, play_type
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.why: The attempt-count factor for the 70+ field goal contract: with no attempts at 68+ yards the longest-FG market cannot move, so this isolates the decision stage from leg strength.

nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.label: Extreme-value tail fit for play length (long plays and long kicks)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.mechanism: Generalized Pareto or Gumbel-type fit to the upper tail of scrimmage-play and kick lengths, giving return levels for the league-wide season maximum.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.rationale: The contract is a threshold on a maximum, so only the extreme tail matters. A bulk model (mean yards per play) is nearly irrelevant, and the cap of 99 yards plus the finite number of own-goal-line snaps means a bounded-tail fit with exposure weighting is required. Few historical points mean parameter uncertainty must be carried into the probability.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.measurement: Using all regular-season plays since 1999, fit a peaks-over-threshold model (threshold 60 yards for plays, 56 yards for kick distance) with Poisson exceedance rate per 1,000 snaps by start-yardline bucket and an era term (pre-2024, 2024, 2025+ kicking rules) on the kick tail; fit offensive gains and turnover-return lengths separately so either contract reading can be priced; propagate parameter uncertainty by posterior or bootstrap; output P(max >= 99) and P(max kick >= 70) for N remaining games with the running maximum to date as the as-of state.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference longest-play and longest-FG record lists (free, scrape)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.why: Provides the statistical backbone for both threshold contracts and the sanity check on the exposure-times-conversion decomposition.

nfl.td_play_length_by_source.label: Touchdown play length by source (scrimmage, interception, fumble, kick and punt return, missed-FG return)
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.mechanism: Distribution of touchdown lengths split by scoring route, because returns can exceed 99 yards and short touchdowns come from goal-line runs and sneaks.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.rationale: The single-game TD-length buckets read official play-by-play distances and do not exclude returns, so the route mix matters: return TDs reach 100-109 yards, while fumbles recovered in the end zone give 0-yard TDs that can set the minimum. Season-wide the minimum is almost always 0-1 yards, but per game it depends on how many TDs are scored and how.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.measurement: From 1999-2026 regular-season plays with a touchdown, assign route: scrimmage (pass or rush; length = yards_gained), interception return, fumble return, kickoff return, punt return, missed/blocked FG return (length = return_yards, kick returns measured from the receiving spot as yardline of catch to goal). Tabulate counts per season and route, per-season maximum and minimum, and rate per 1,000 snaps of that route type (kicks per team kick). Fit per route a generalized Pareto above its 80th percentile length (peaks-over-threshold as in nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit). Output both aggregates with and without return TDs so either contract reading can be priced.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.why: Needed to price KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD readings under return-inclusive and scrimmage-only definitions.

nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.label: Long turnover-return tail on scrimmage downs (99+ yard INT, fumble, blocked/missed-FG returns)
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.mechanism: Interceptions and fumbles in the defence's own red zone, and missed or blocked field goals fielded in the end zone, can be returned 99-109 yards on a play that began as a scrimmage down.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.rationale: If Kalshi counts these as plays from scrimmage, they are a more frequent route to 99+ yards than offensive gains from the own 1 and the own-1 exposure is no longer a bound. Exposure is opponent red-zone and goal-line pass attempts and long FG attempts, not own-1 snaps.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.measurement: Per team-game, rate of returns >= 99 yards on interceptions, fumbles and missed/blocked FGs from nflverse pbp (return_yards, play_type, interception, fumble_lost, field_goal_result) since 1999; exposure = opponent snaps with yardline_100 <= 10 plus FG attempts of 50+ yards; hierarchical Poisson with team takeaway rate shrunk to league (40 team-games prior); output expected count for remaining games.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.why: Under the return-inclusive reading of 'play from scrimmage', 99+ yard interception, fumble and missed or blocked FG returns are a second, more frequent route to YES.

nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.label: Kicking-ball and field-goal rule era (K-ball preparation, fair-catch kick, kickoff regime)
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.mechanism: Rule changes may alter ball flight and attempt opportunities: a 2025 rule letting kickers prepare kicking balls is reported (secondary news only; primary rulebook not fetched; UNVERIFIED) to have been followed by a jump in 60+ yard makes, and the fair-catch free kick is described as allowing an unrushed attempt scored as a field goal (UNVERIFIED).
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.rationale: A tail fit pooled over 1999-2024 understates the current 70+ rate unless an era term is added; the post-2025 sample is small, so the era effect must be estimated with a prior and carried as uncertainty.
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.measurement: Era indicator per season (pre-2024, 2024 dynamic kickoff, 2025+ K-ball preparation and touchback-to-35); estimate era-specific 60+ attempt rate per team-game and make rate by distance from pbp with a hierarchical prior centred on the previous era (half the era difference as prior sd); flag fair-catch free kicks separately from scrimmage FGs; as-of = league rulebook for the season.
free_sources: NFL rulebook and competition committee announcements (free)
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.why: Rule changes (2025 kicking-ball preparation, fair-catch free kick, kickoff regime) shift the 60+ and 70+ yard attempt and make rates, so tail fits need an era term.

nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.label: Preseason and warm-up long-kick evidence (60+ yard makes outside the regular season)
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.mechanism: Preseason makes and reported warm-up distances reveal a kicker's ceiling without the regular-season attempt selection that hides it.
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.rationale: Only a handful of regular-season attempts exceed 65 yards, so the leg ceiling is nearly unidentified from settlement-scope data; a 70-yard preseason make (2025) is the only direct evidence a 70 is reachable. Preseason kicks are out of scope for settlement but in scope as an input.
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.measurement: Per kicker, list preseason FG attempts of 55+ yards with result, venue, roof and wind from preseason play-by-play (seasons 2015+), plus beat-reported warm-up makes with date; summarise as max make and makes at 60+ and 65+; feed to the ceiling tail at half weight per attempt; as-of = last preseason game or report timestamp.
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play preseason games (season_type PRE, coverage unverified)
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.why: Preseason and warm-up long makes are out of settlement scope but are the only direct evidence that a kicker can reach 70 yards.

nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.label: Single-game touchdown-length order statistics (P(max >= k), P(min in band), P(no TD))
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.mechanism: The longest and shortest TD of a game are the max and min of N TD lengths, N random per game and each length drawn from a route mixture (goal-line, red-zone pass, explosive scrimmage, return or recovery).
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.rationale: Bucket markets need the whole distribution of the max and min, not a mean: the count N moves the two tails in opposite directions, zero TDs is a NO for all buckets, and integer yards with inclusive bounds create discreteness at 5/6 and 10/11 yards.
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.measurement: For each team, N_TD ~ negative binomial with mean from nfl.model_team_td_mean (market-free) and dispersion fit on 2015+ games; per TD, route probabilities from goal-to-go share (nfl.redzone, nfl.goal_line_personnel) and non-offensive TD hazard (nfl.dst_td_hazard); length per route from the empirical 2015+ distribution of official TD distances shrunk to league with 30 TDs per team prior. Simulate 20,000 games; output bucket probabilities and P(N=0).
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.why: Max and min of the touchdown lengths in one game settle KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD buckets, including the zero-TD NO mass.

nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.label: Player single-game longest reception model (max of K catches vs strike)
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.mechanism: P(longest reception > strike | plays) = 1 - E[F(strike)^K], where K is the number of receptions and F the player's per-catch length CDF in this matchup.
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.rationale: The contract ignores total yards: one long catch settles YES and zero catches settles NO, so volume enters through K and the upper tail of per-catch length matters more than the mean. Active-no-play settles at the fair price, so the forecastable part is conditional on a live snap.
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.measurement: K ~ negative binomial: targets forecast (nfl.targets) times catch probability (nfl.catch_rate_oe), dispersion fit on last 2 seasons; per-catch length = air yards (nfl.air_yards_adot, depth mixture) plus YAC, from the player's last 24 games with half-life 8 games, shrunk to position-role with 60 catches prior, adjusted by coverage matchup; compute 1 - sum_k P(K=k) F(s)^k at each strike; multiply by 1 - P(no live snap | active).
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play (receiver_player_id, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards, yards_after_catch)
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.why: KXNFLLONGREC settles on a player's single longest catch in a game, the max over a random number of receptions.

nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.reason: Closest existing model for the 70+ field goal series, but stops at 50+ and 60+ and cannot extrapolate beyond the demonstrated range alone.

nfl.kicker.reason: Accuracy by distance and career max are useful; kickoff touchback depth is a leg proxy only within one kickoff-rule era (2024+ kickoffs are strategic), and accuracy under 55 yards does not decide a 70.

nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.reason: 20+ and 40+ yard rates describe the bulk of the long tail; the 99-yard event is far beyond it and needs the own-1 start conditioning.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.reason: Explosive-run tail by rusher informs one of two ways a scrimmage play can go 99, but runs rarely start at the own 1 in open space.

nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.reason: Includes longest-play probability by receiver, useful for who completes a deep shot; the player-level frame misses the exposure count.

nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.reason: Counts snaps near the own goal line; for a 99-yard play only the own-1 snap matters, so it adds no signal beyond the own-1 rate except as a cross-check.

nfl.venue.reason: Altitude and roof directly change kick range; irrelevant for scrimmage plays beyond surface speed.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind at kickoff vintages decides whether a 66-70 yard kick is reachable; secondary for the scrimmage contract.

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.reason: Mid-field fourth-down policy is adjacent to, but weaker than, the end-of-half attempt policy that actually yields 68+ yard kicks.

nfl.penalties.reason: Rules text excludes nullified plays, so flag rate on long gains is a real subtractive factor but a modest one.

nfl.season_to_date_pace.reason: Running maximum to date and games left are an absorbing state: a single qualifying event settles the season contracts, so this is the primary as-of input.

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Only matters through kicker and QB availability; the extremes are league-wide so one absence rarely moves the probability.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules define regular-season scope, the 99-yard play definition, the penalty exclusion, the zero-TD NO rule, inclusive TD buckets and the active-no-play fair price; all five series have sampled text.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled values and timestamps verify the record but add no forecasting signal.

m.stat_correction_risk.reason: Corrections to yardage or kick distance could change a threshold outcome and the rules name official stats as the source.

nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.reason: Supplies the era flag that decides whether kickoff depth can proxy leg power and how return-TD lengths pool across seasons.

nfl.model_team_td_mean.reason: Market-free TD mean per team sets N in the single-game TD max/min and the zero-TD probability that resolves every bucket NO.

nfl.redzone.reason: Goal-to-go conversion sets the share of short TDs, which decides the shortest-TD bucket; weak for the longest-TD bucket.

nfl.goal_line_personnel.reason: Sneak versus short run versus play action inside the 5 shifts short TD lengths between 1-2 and 3-5 yards, relevant to minimum buckets.

nfl.dst_td_hazard.reason: Defensive and return TDs are either very long or zero yards, so they move both tails of single-game TD length.

nfl.targets.reason: Target volume is the count the longest reception is a maximum over; low-target players carry a large zero-catch NO mass.

nfl.air_yards_adot.reason: Depth of target sets the per-catch length distribution; deep-target share drives the upper tail that the over-strike settles on.

nfl.catch_rate_oe.reason: Converts targets to catches and gives YAC over expected; both enter the max-of-K calculation but are noisy at player level.

nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.reason: Active-no-live-play settles at the pre-game fair price, so this probability sets how much of the payoff is forecastable at all.

nfl.inactives_pit.reason: Fixes active status 90 minutes before kickoff; the inactive case is not described in the sampled rules, so its effect is uncertain (u6).

nfl.cb_coverage_matchup.reason: Shadow coverage shifts the receiver's per-catch length distribution but public alignment proxies are weak.

interactions.mechanism: Expected number of 70+ makes is attempts at that range times make probability, so either factor near zero keeps the sum near zero; a strong-legged kicker on a coach who prefers a Hail Mary adds almost nothing, and a coach willing to try with a kicker below range adds only misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected 70+ makes per team as the product of the two factors and compare with a model that sums them; check that the product model ranks past 64+ yard attempts better.

interactions.mechanism: Altitude (thinner air) plus a strong following wind adds several effective yards; a kicker with a 66-yard ceiling reaches 70 only when both help, which happens only outdoors in a few venues and weeks. Domes remove wind entirely, so indoor kicks get neither the tailwind gain nor the altitude gain except in a high-altitude dome.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate make probability at 62+ yards with a venue-by-wind interaction term and test the slope above 15 mph tailwind versus roof or sea-level venues.

interactions.mechanism: The 99-yard play is Poisson thinning: exposure count times conversion; uncertainty in the count and the tail compounds, and snaps cluster by team and week, so the joint distribution is wider than independent factors imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate remaining games with a negative binomial exposure and a Beta conversion, and compare predictive intervals with a product-of-point-estimates calculation on historical seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Long plays from deep starts carry a high chance of a holding flag or a rarer illegal block, which the rules exclude; the nullification share is conditional on play length and the offence's penalty profile, so it lowers the conversion more for teams that hold often.
interactions.how_to_test: From historical 50+ yard gains, estimate the nullification rate by length bucket and team penalty rate, then test whether it rises with yards gained.

interactions.mechanism: Once games are played without an event, remaining exposure shrinks, so the probability of YES decays toward zero in the last weeks, while any past event resolves it; the response of P(YES) to games left is exponential not linear.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest the hazard decay on prior seasons conditioned on no event before week N, comparing a constant-rate model with the thinned count.

interactions.mechanism: The TD count moves the longest-TD and shortest-TD buckets in opposite directions at once: a high-scoring game raises P(max >= 51) and lowers the minimum toward 1-2 yards, while a one-TD game sets max = min. Buckets across the two series are therefore correlated through N.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2015+ games, compare observed P(max >= 51) and P(min in 6-10) by realised TD count with the order-statistic model, and test the correlation of the two bucket outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that the longest catch beats the strike is 1 - F^K, which rises steeply from zero to three catches and flattens after; an extra target matters a lot for a low-volume tight end and little for a high-volume WR1.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin player-games by receptions and plot the observed rate of longest reception above 16.5 yards; fit 1 - F^K against a linear-in-targets model.

interactions.mechanism: Under the offence-only reading the 99-yard probability is driven by own-1 snaps alone; under the return-inclusive reading long turnover returns dominate. The contract interpretation switches which exposure matters, so the price of the series depends on u5.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute season P(YES) under each reading from 1999-2025 history and report both; check past Kalshi settlements or rule clarifications for any return-yard event.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic collapse of make probability beyond about 63-65 yards
nonlinearities.why: Make probability falls from near 40 percent at 60 yards to a small tail past 66, so a few yards of kicker or wind help changes the 70+ probability by multiples, not by an additive amount.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold with saturation in tailwind speed; zero effect in domes
nonlinearities.why: Wind adds distance only after it exceeds roughly 10-15 mph and its effect is capped by the kick trajectory; roof games get zero tailwind benefit, so the response is piecewise, not linear.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating exponent: P(at least one) = 1 - exp(-rate x games)
nonlinearities.why: The contract settles on at least one event, so the probability saturates as the expected count grows and is nearly linear only when the count is small.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at zero TDs plus order-statistic tails that sharpen with N
nonlinearities.why: P(max >= 51) grows roughly like 1 - (1 - p)^N and P(min in 6-10) falls as N grows, with all buckets NO at N = 0, so bucket probabilities are not linear in expected points.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave saturation in receptions K: 1 - F(s)^K
nonlinearities.why: Each extra catch adds less to P(longest > strike); with zero catches the probability is exactly zero, so the response to target volume is steep at low volume and flat at high volume.

catalog_entry.label: NFL Draft and Supplemental Draft selection markets
contract_types: Draft pick slot (1st overall, exact selection, team making a pick)
Team draft by position or round (incl. position of team's first pick)
Draft comparison and matchup (prospect vs prospect, school with most picks)
School draftee count over the whole draft
catalog_entry.target: Probability a named prospect is selected at a slot, range or positional order, or a team makes/uses a given pick, per the official Draft results.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Draft outcomes come from a deterministic order process (season results, tiebreakers, compensatory awards and trades decide who holds each of about 257 slots over seven rounds) combined with team decisions among prospects: each team picks from a board shaped by consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits, subject to the prospect being eligible, declaring and passing medicals. Trades break the order; positional order statistics, school counts and team-round outcomes are correlated across prospects, so a joint all-rounds simulation is required.

inputs.why: Consensus rankings, draft order and team needs are the baseline of every draft selection contract.
Race for the worst record and strength-of-schedule tiebreak decides who holds the first pick and the order of the top slots.
QB-class order, team need and trade-up model feed quarterback-order contracts.
Maps results to round-one slots (KXNFLDRAFTSELECT's 32nd pick, KXNFLDRAFT1ST's 1st pick); later-round order comes from the full-order input.
Resolves the team-level contract rule that a traded pick resolves to the team that actually selects, and drives pick-slot markets for named prospects.
Converts a ranking into the probabilities that top-5, exact-slot, over/under and Nth-at-position contracts actually settle on.
Drives which position a pick holder drafts: the main team-side term in position-drafted, team-draft-by-position and QB-order contracts.
Every named-prospect contract carries the pre-condition that the player is in the pool; the hurdle is largest in the months before the declaration deadline.
The position and trade behavior of the picking team is the part that a consensus ranking cannot supply.
Settlement of the QB-order and position-drafted series depends on which source's label counts for hybrid players.
Needed for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP, a separate mechanism from the April draft that no consensus board models.
Season simulation distribution supplies the uncertainty in final standings that sets slots and the 31st and 32nd picks.
Tiebreaker resolution (strength of schedule, then division and conference tiebreaks) among tied records, which the order rules need and the win-count simulation does not provide.
Timestamped reporting about team intentions, prospect visits and medical updates moves the pick distribution.
Cap room and contract guarantees decide whether a team can afford a rookie slot or a veteran QB.
Roster turnover and returning production indicate positional holes and need.
A coaching or GM change resets draft philosophy and quarterback need.
Draft-capital prior for unproven quarterbacks measures how a team views an incumbent against a rookie.
Draft-week and draft-night insider reports are the main late information for exact-slot and team markets that stay open into the draft; their hit rate by outlet sets the weight.
Calendar of the combine, declaration deadline and draft night structures when information arrives.
Reference-class frequency for rare procedural events (a Supplemental Draft being held, a draft postponed), used only where no draft-specific history exists.
Wording on traded picks, positions and which draft counts defines settlement for each series.
Markets close at the draft; knowing the timing avoids look-ahead and sets valid information cutoffs.
Official draft results and position labels used to verify settlement.
Seven-round order with compensatory picks fixes the last pick (KXNFLLASTPICKPOS), round-3 boundaries (KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS, KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE) and pick 64 (KXNFLDRAFTOU).
League eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings and NIL-era return incentives gate whether named prospects are in the pool at all.
Per-school pool of draft-eligible prospects with projected rounds drives KXNFLDRAFTCAT counts and the KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE school argmax.

interactions.hypothesis: A team with a high quarterback need but a later pick trades up, so need raises the quarterback's slot only if the holder will move.
The gap between the top two quarterbacks and the class depth set the order and the quarterback premium over consensus.
The slot distribution is the season simulation passed through the order rules, so the 32nd pick is a Super Bowl winner distribution, not a record ranking.
A school's count of picks is a sum of correlated per-prospect draft events; slot dispersion around round boundaries decides counts in rounds 1-3.

contract.settlement_definition: Twenty-five live series, twenty-three with sampled rules (all but KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK). Named-prospect slot series: KXNFLDRAFT1/KXNFLDRAFTPICK (selected 1st overall), KXNFLDRAFTTOP (drafted top 5), KXNFLDRAFTOU (drafted in the first 64 picks), KXNFLDRAFTMATCHUP (drafted first of two named players). Nth-at-position series (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DT, Edge, LB, DB) use the Governing League's position when sources differ. Team series: KXNFLDRAFT1ST and KXNFLDRAFTSELECT settle on the team that ultimately makes the 1st/32nd selection after trades; KXNFLDRAFTTEAM on the selecting team (undrafted = NO); KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS (QB in rounds 1-3) and KXNFLTEAM1POS (position of the team's first pick). Aggregates: KXNFLDRAFTCAT (at least N players of a school in the whole draft) and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE (school with most picks in rounds 1-3, ties paid 1/N) on the league's college classification; KXNFLLASTPICKPOS on the position of the last player selected. KXNFLSDRAFTTOP: named player selected at any point in the Supplemental Draft. KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK have no listing.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK have no listing or rules; by title they appear to duplicate KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS and KXNFLDRAFT1, but settlement wording is unverified.

Undrafted = NO is written only for KXNFLDRAFTTEAM; for exact-slot, top-5, over/under, matchup and Nth-at-position series the NO case for a non-declaring or undrafted player is inferred, and the matchup case where neither player is drafted is unstated (u7).
Position series use the league position at selection (DB = cornerback or safety; OL = tackle, guard or center; Edge separate from DT and LB), so hybrid labels shift the ordinal count.
KXNFLLASTPICKPOS and KXNFLDRAFTCAT depend on round 7 and compensatory picks; KXNFLDRAFTOU and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE on the round-2/round-3 boundaries, not only on round one.
The same prospect appears in a finalized 2026 first-pick market and in 2027 QB-order and top-5 markets, so pool membership can cross a draft year through eligibility decisions.
Draft postponement or cancellation, and a Supplemental Draft not being held, are not addressed in any sampled text (u8).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league draft results and position labels; Kalshi cites the Governing League and Source Agencies. Draft-night announcements are the primary record.

mechanism.summary: A draft selection outcome is generated by a chain: eligibility rules and declaration decisions fix the pool; season results, tiebreakers and compensatory awards fix the seven-round order; trades reassign who holds slots; and each pick-holder chooses from a board mixing consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits. Ordinal contracts (3rd quarterback, top five, before pick 64), school counts and team-round outcomes are functions of correlated choices, so one team's decision at pick 2 changes every later probability. Consensus rank gives the centre of each prospect's slot distribution, but position premiums, trades and thin late-round boards give skewed, heavy-tailed errors, so the unit of analysis is a joint simulation of all rounds.

stages.name: Eligibility and gating: who is in the pool
stages.description: A prospect must be league-eligible (three seasons removed from high school), still have or have exhausted NCAA eligibility as courts and waivers decide, choose to declare rather than return under NIL and revenue-sharing pay, and clear medical and character checks. In November declaration is months away and these gates dominate named-prospect contracts for underclass quarterbacks; for the Supplemental Draft eligibility is a league ruling on a petition, and the draft itself may not be held.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per prospect with a strong prior by projected round; late shocks from injury

stages.name: Order formation: standings and tiebreakers to slots
stages.description: Final standings and playoff results are mapped to round-one slots (worst record first with strength-of-schedule tiebreak, playoff teams by round exited, Super Bowl loser 31 and winner 32) and repeated each round, with compensatory picks (announced in March) appended to rounds 3-7. The order is unknown in November, so each slot is a distribution from a season simulation, and forfeitures or compensatory awards shift overall numbering and the identity of the final pick.
stages.distribution: Discrete slot distribution with fat tails for playoff teams; exact once the season ends

stages.name: Team choice: boards, need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits
stages.description: Each pick-holder selects from its board. Consensus value sets the initial ordering, positional need and the quarterback regime tilt choices (a holder with no franchise QB near the top of the class faces strong pressure), and GM and coach habits determine reach tendency, trade-down frequency and how positions like EDGE are valued.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice among a few candidates with team-specific heterogeneity

stages.name: Trades and reshuffling before and on draft night
stages.description: Teams trade up for a quarterback or a rare talent and trade down for assets; each trade changes the team that makes a given pick and the demand curve for later slots. Trade-up hazard depends on the consensus gap between the prospect and the next, the buyer's pick stock and need, and the seller's willingness, and it is partly reported by insiders ahead of time.
stages.distribution: Rare but high-impact jumps; conditional on gap and need

stages.name: Realization, labelling and settlement
stages.description: Selections are announced on draft night and settle from the official record: slot, team, and the position label given by the league. Hybrid labels (edge versus linebacker) and Nth-at-position rules depend on that label; markets close at the draft, so information vintage must stop before the first selection.
stages.distribution: Deterministic after the draft; label disagreement risk at position boundaries

stages.name: School aggregates: draftee counts and the rounds 1-3 school argmax
stages.description: KXNFLDRAFTCAT counts one school's players over all seven rounds and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE asks which school has the most picks in rounds 1-3, with ties paid 1/N. A school's count is a sum of correlated per-prospect events: whether each senior and underclassman declares, whether he is drafted at all, and whether his slot falls before the round-3 boundary. Elite programs place 8-14 players, so the count is concentrated near a threshold and ties at the top are common.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial sum of dependent Bernoullis per school; discrete with frequent ties at the argmax; truncated by declarations

stages.name: Deep-round slots and team positional choices across rounds
stages.description: KXNFLLASTPICKPOS settles on the position of the final overall selection (a compensatory round-7 slot), KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS on whether a team takes a quarterback in rounds 1-3, and KXNFLTEAM1POS on the position of a team's first selection, which depends on whether it still owns its round-one pick. Late-round choices follow team need, special-teams value and positional scarcity rather than consensus boards, which thin out beyond about 150 prospects.
stages.distribution: Categorical position outcome with flat late-round priors; team-round events are Bernoulli conditional on pick inventory

talent_strength.note: Prospect quality as consensus value and team results that fix the order.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent; the competition is the other pick holders in order, whose decisions are covered through team need, ownership and slot-dispersion inputs rather than a matchup variable.

role_personnel.note: Starter quality and depth by position and quarterback regime determine needs.

availability_news.note: Eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings, NIL-era declaration choice, medicals and timestamped reports.

coaching_scheme.note: GM and coach habits and regime changes shape position valuation and trading.

environment.note: No venue, weather or surface exists in a selection meeting; draft-night location and crowd have no mechanism that moves who is selected.

game_context_script.note: The draft-night sequence (trades, clock, run on a position) plays the role of game flow.

pace_volume.note: Number of selections per round including compensatory picks and forfeits is the volume the counts and last-pick markets run over.

efficiency_conversion.note: Rate at which insider reports and consensus rank convert to the realized pick.

distribution_variance.note: Heavy-tailed slot errors, order-statistic dependence among prospects and tie-prone school counts.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tanking incentives, late-season stakes and the calendar of deadlines.

officiating_rules.note: Draft-order and compensatory rules, the league eligibility rule and Supplemental Draft procedures play the rules role.

settlement_contract.note: Traded-pick rule, league position label and series with no rules.

nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.label: Draft order rules engine (season result to overall slot)
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.mechanism: Deterministic mapping from final standings, playoff results and tiebreakers to round-one overall slots 1-32 (champion 32, Super Bowl loser 31), repeated in each round; compensatory picks and later rounds are handled by nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.rationale: Slot ownership before the draft is not a model output but a rules calculation on results that are still uncertain in November: non-playoff teams are ordered by record then strength of schedule, playoff teams by round exited, so the 32nd pick equals the Super Bowl winner. Forfeitures can shorten a round and shift overall numbering.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.measurement: Implement league draft-order rules: non-playoff teams ascending by win percentage, ties broken by strength of schedule then divisional and conference tiebreakers; picks 19-24 wild card losers, 25-28 divisional losers, 29-30 conference-final losers, 31 Super Bowl loser, 32 champion; apply the league's list of forfeited picks. Run on simulated seasons from the season simulation to give the slot distribution per team; as-of = latest game result and the official pick-transaction list.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.why: KXNFLDRAFTSELECT settles on the team making the 32nd overall pick, which is the Super Bowl winner under these rules unless the pick was traded; slot 1 is set by the worst record.

nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.label: Draft pick ownership and trade graph (who holds each slot, trade-up hazard)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.mechanism: Current owner of each first-round pick, the set of future-pick bundles, and the chance a slot changes hands before or on draft night.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.rationale: Contracts settle on the team that ultimately makes the pick and on pick-order outcomes, so ownership at the moment of selection is the relevant variable. Trade-ups for a quarterback, by a team that holds a later pick, are the main way that consensus order is broken, and there is a documented pre-draft window when picks are exchanged.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.measurement: Maintain a table of pick-by-pick ownership for all seven rounds with transaction timestamps; estimate P(slot k traded before selection) with a logistic on slot, consensus gap between the top prospects, holder's quarterback need and asset stock, fitted on the last 15 drafts with shrinkage toward the empirical draft-wide trade rate for the same slot band (estimated, no fixed prior asserted); as-of = the latest official trade list.
free_sources: Over The Cap / Spotrac pick ownership (free_limited)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.why: Resolves the team-level contract rule that a traded pick resolves to the team that actually selects, and drives pick-slot markets for named prospects.

nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.label: Prospect slot dispersion model (consensus rank to realized pick distribution)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.mechanism: Empirical distribution of realized pick minus consensus rank by rank band and position, giving heavy-tailed, skewed slot distributions that vary by position premium.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.rationale: Consensus boards give a central ranking, but markets ask for ordinal events (1st overall, top 5, before pick N, 3rd quarterback). The spread of realized slot around consensus grows with rank, is asymmetric for quarterbacks (they are taken early) and depends on how close the point-in-time board was to the draft.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.measurement: From 2010-2026 drafts (seven rounds) join consensus rank (mean of public big boards dated 90, 30 and 1 days before the draft; exclude mock drafts and any source that cites sportsbook odds) to realized pick. Fit ordinal logistic regression of draft-pick bucket (1-32 by pick, then round buckets) plus an undrafted category on log(rank), position (QB, EDGE, OT, other) and days-to-draft, with spread parameter rising with rank; shrink thin positions toward the pooled model with weight 20 draftees. Output a slot PMF over picks 1-257 + undrafted per prospect; cross-prospect order statistics by sampling slots sequentially without replacement. As-of the board vintage date.
free_sources: NFL Mock Draft Database (free, scrape; historical vintage needs own capture)
raw_data: consensus rank by date (90, 30, 1 days pre-draft)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.why: Converts a ranking into the probabilities that top-5, exact-slot, over/under and Nth-at-position contracts actually settle on.

nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.label: Team positional need and quarterback regime (who needs what at their slot)
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.mechanism: A per-team, per-position need score from starters' age, contract end, production and offseason moves, plus a quarterback state (franchise QB, bridge, none, draft-and-develop).
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.rationale: Slot buyers choose among a handful of boards; need breaks ties between near-equal prospects and sets quarterback pressure: a top-3 holder without a franchise QB faces a qualitatively different incentive than a holder with a long-term deal. Free agency and trades before the draft shift need so a stale vintage is wrong.
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.measurement: Need score per team-position = 0.30 x starter age percentile above position median (0-1) + 0.25 x [years remaining <= 1] + 0.25 x (1 - last-season EPA-based percentile of the starter at the position from nflverse, no PFF) + 0.20 x depth gap (1 if no starter-grade player is under contract after free agency). QB regime codes: 0 = long-term starter (guarantees through next 2 seasons), 1 = bridge/short deal, 2 = no starter-grade QB, plus a flag for QB drafted in rounds 1-2 within 2 years. Shrink position-group means with weight 10 team-years. Weights are assumptions to be fit by regression on historical first-round position choices. Refresh weekly until the draft; as-of last transaction.
free_sources: nflverse rosters, depth charts and contracts (free)
raw_data: roster and depth chart by position
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.why: Drives which position a pick holder drafts: the main team-side term in position-drafted, team-draft-by-position and QB-order contracts.

nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.label: Prospect declaration, eligibility and medical status
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.mechanism: Whether a named prospect enters the draft pool at all, remains draft-eligible, and passes medicals, testing and character gates before the draft.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.rationale: A named-prospect contract resolves NO if the player returns to college, is ruled ineligible or falls to a medical and disciplinary red flag. In November the declaration is still months away, the NCAA season is in progress and injuries during the college season change draft value; the deadline for underclassmen is known but the choices are not.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.measurement: P(declare) per underclass prospect by logistic regression on early-entry outcomes of 2021-2026 classes (NIL era, fitted separately from 2010-2020) with features class year, position, consensus round bucket (1, 2-3, 4-7, undrafted) from nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model, consensus-rank percentile, and an injury flag = 1 if the player missed 4+ games in either of the last two seasons from team injury reports or beat reports; ridge lambda by CV. Add post-combine/pro-day update: replace round bucket by the updated consensus rank. P(in pool) = P(declare) for eligible players, 1 for exhausted-eligibility seniors. As-of the last official list or the player's dated statement; no market data.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.why: Every named-prospect contract carries the pre-condition that the player is in the pool; the hurdle is largest in the months before the declaration deadline.

nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General manager and head coach draft behavior history
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Per decision-maker record of trading down, trading up for quarterbacks, positional reaches versus consensus, and tenure resets when GM or coach changes.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: The picks are made by a small number of people with persistent habits: some GMs trade down 40 percent of the time, others take the best available; a new GM or coach resets need and scheme (4-3 versus 3-4 edge definition). Reaches above consensus rank are a stable personal trait.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: For each GM and head coach, compute (a) trade-down and trade-up frequency by round, (b) mean reach versus consensus rank by position in rounds 1-3, (c) positions drafted by round including late-round special-teams and positional-value habits, using their past 5 drafts with tenure weighting and shrinkage to the league mean with 3 drafts of prior weight; flag new decision makers and set a new-regime weight to the franchise's last regime at 50 percent.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.why: The position and trade behavior of the picking team is the part that a consensus ranking cannot supply.

nfl.draft_position_label_governance.label: Draft position label governance (official position classification)
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.mechanism: Mapping from a prospect to the position label that settles contracts (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DL, EDGE, LB, DB), including how the governing league and source agencies label hybrid players.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.rationale: Position-drafted and Nth-at-position contracts depend on labels, and the rules text states that if positions differ across source agencies the Governing League's position is used. Edge rushers, hybrid linebackers and safeties-cornerbacks and tackle-guard swaps are exactly where labels diverge.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.measurement: Build a label table from the league's draft tracker position at the time of selection and compare with the college and consensus-board labels for the last 10 classes; compute the disagreement rate by position pair (EDGE versus DL versus LB, S versus CB, OT versus OG) and carry it as probability mass into Nth-at-position markets; as-of = each pick announcement.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.why: Settlement of the QB-order and position-drafted series depends on which source's label counts for hybrid players.

nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.label: Supplemental Draft mechanics (eligibility petition, tiered lottery order, bid cost)
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.mechanism: Supplemental Draft eligibility via petition, an order set by a lottery within record-based tiers (non-playoff teams grouped by wins, then playoff teams), and the bid rule that costs a team its same-round pick in the next regular draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.rationale: This draft is held rarely and picks only the few players the league declares eligible; whether a named player is selected depends on whether any team will pay a future pick, so the key variables are eligibility ruling, the player's expected round and team needs, not consensus board ranking.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.measurement: Count Supplemental Draft years with and without picks over 1977-2026 for a base rate; model P(selected) per eligible player from projected round (a bid costs the same-round pick next year, so teams bid only if the player is worth it), team round-pick inventory, and the league ruling date; as-of = league announcement of eligibility and the date of the draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.why: Needed for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP, a separate mechanism from the April draft that no consensus board models.

nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.label: Full seven-round draft order with compensatory picks (who holds each of about 257 selections)
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.mechanism: Round-by-round order repeats the round-one order, with compensatory selections (awarded in March under the free-agency formula and special minority-hiring picks) appended at the ends of rounds 3-7 and forfeitures removed; the last of these is the final selection.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.rationale: The last-pick, school-count, rounds 1-3 and pick-64 series settle beyond round one, where ownership depends on compensatory awards and late trades. Before March the number and placement of compensatory picks are uncertain, so the identity and team of the last pick is a distribution.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.measurement: Build rounds 1-7 from the rules engine order; forecast compensatory picks per team from net free-agent losses and the public compensatory formula projections until the official March release, then use the official list; apply forfeits and traded-pick ownership; output, per slot, the holding team distribution and the overall pick number of round boundaries (end of round 2, end of round 3) and of the final selection.
free_sources: NFL official compensatory pick release (free, March)
Over The Cap compensatory pick projections (free_limited)
raw_data: official seven-round order with compensatory flags
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.why: Seven-round order with compensatory picks fixes the last pick (KXNFLLASTPICKPOS), round-3 boundaries (KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS, KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE) and pick 64 (KXNFLDRAFTOU).

nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.label: Prospect eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility case status and NIL-era declare incentive
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.mechanism: The league requires three seasons since high school graduation; NCAA eligibility waivers and litigation can grant extra college seasons; NIL and revenue-sharing pay raise the value of returning, strongest for quarterbacks.
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.rationale: For early enrollees and reclassified prospects the league clock can bar entry regardless of talent, and pending eligibility rulings decide whether a player stays in college; a pre-NIL declare base rate overstates entry for top underclass QBs. These gates dominate named-prospect 2027 markets in November.
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.measurement: Per prospect compute first eligible draft year = year in which three full seasons have elapsed since high-school graduation. Eligibility flag E = 1 if first eligible year <= target draft year. Extra-year risk X = P(player receives additional college eligibility via waiver or court ruling) = 1 if ruling announced, else base rate from 2021-2026 cases (decided cases won / filed, Beta(1,1) prior) when a case is pending, else 0. P(in pool) = E x (1 - X) x P(declare | NIL era, position, consensus round) from nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_medical's model. As-of: timestamp of latest ruling, statement or early-entry list.
raw_data: high school graduation and college enrolment dates
NCAA eligibility rulings and case dockets
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.why: League eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings and NIL-era return incentives gate whether named prospects are in the pool at all.

nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.label: School draftable-prospect pool (eligible players by school with projected round)
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.mechanism: Count and quality of each school's draft-eligible players (seniors, declared underclassmen, transfers listed under the school the league uses) with per-player probability of being drafted and of going in rounds 1-3.
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.rationale: School count and school argmax series are sums over many prospects, including late-round players that national boards barely rank; transfer-portal moves change the classification school, and the league's college label settles the count.
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.measurement: Per school S: for each eligible prospect i, P(drafted_i) and P(round<=3_i) from nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model; prospects outside the top 300 of the consensus board get position-specific base rates by school tier (power-conference top-25, other power, group of five, FCS) from 2015-2026 drafts. Simulate 20,000 classes: draw one school-level shock z_S ~ N(0, 0.35^2) on the logit of each prospect's probability (sd refit so the cross-school variance of round-1-3 counts matches 2015-2026), then draw selections independently; output P(count >= N) and P(school has max rounds 1-3 count, ties by 1/k split). As-of latest early-entry list.
free_sources: NFL Mock Draft Database consensus boards (free_scrape)
raw_data: prospect list by school and class
historical draftees by school and round
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.why: Per-school pool of draft-eligible prospects with projected rounds drives KXNFLDRAFTCAT counts and the KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE school argmax.

nfl.cap_and_contract.reason: Cap room and contract guarantees affect rookie-slot affordability and veteran-QB substitutes.

nfl.roster_continuity.reason: Turnover and returning production hint at positional holes; used in the team-choice stage as a secondary signal behind the depth-chart need score.

nfl.coach_exit_hazard.reason: A new coach or GM resets draft behavior; the hazard itself only matters if it resolves before the draft.

nfl.qb_challenger_prior.reason: Draft-capital value gap for QBs is informative about team QB regime but is a season-level, not draft-specific, signal.

nfl.insider_report_conversion.reason: Draft-week and draft-night insider reports are the main late information for exact-slot and team markets open into the draft; hit rates by outlet set their weight.

nfl.event_calendar_hazard.reason: Calendar of events structures when information arrives; it does not change who is picked.

nfl.offfield_base_rate.reason: Generic off-field base rates matter only for rare procedural events such as a Supplemental Draft being held or a draft postponed; draft-specific history dominates elsewhere.

m.lifecycle.reason: The market closes at the draft or the announcement, which sets the valid information cutoff.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Official draft results confirm settlement but add no forecast signal.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback-needy team that holds a later pick trades up only when the gap to the top quarterback is large and it holds enough assets, so need raises a quarterback's expected slot only through the trade graph; with a top-3 pick and no quarterback the effect is direct.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized quarterback slots in drafts split by need of the top-5 holders and by presence of a trade-up; test the need effect with and without a trade indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Quarterbacks are drafted earlier than consensus rank and the order among them is correlated: if the first quarterback goes first overall the remaining quarterbacks' slots shift together, so the 3rd-quarterback contract is an order statistic of dependent slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the class with and without a position premium and rank-order correlation and compare with realized orders of quarterbacks in 2010-2026 drafts.

interactions.mechanism: The 32nd pick is the Super Bowl winner and the 1st pick the worst record, so the slot distribution is the extremes of a simulated season: tails dominate and teams that look similar by rating have very different probabilities of the end slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Run the season simulation through the rules engine and compare predicted end-slot distributions with historical pre-playoff projections.

interactions.mechanism: Prospects projected in round one declare almost surely, so declaration risk is a threshold in projected round; below the threshold return-to-school and medical flags dominate and the slot distribution is a mixture with a mass at undrafted.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(declare) against consensus rank at the declaration deadline and test for a step near the first-round boundary.

interactions.mechanism: Team need only converts to a pick when the decision-maker's habit permits it: a GM who rarely reaches ignores need for the best player, while a reach-prone GM acts on need, so the two multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the position drafted on need by GM reach propensity and test the interaction coefficient.

interactions.mechanism: A school's count of picks in rounds 1-3 sums dependent per-player events: a deep positional class at one school competes for the same team needs, and boundary prospects near pick 100 swing the argmax, so counts are overdispersed and ties at the top are frequent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated rounds 1-3 school counts and tie rates against 2010-2026 drafts with and without a shared school-class shock.

interactions.mechanism: Declaration choice only matters once the eligibility clock is satisfied and no extra NCAA season is granted; in the NIL era a top underclass QB with remaining eligibility may return, so the declare probability is conditional on eligibility state and position.
interactions.how_to_test: Split post-2021 early-entry decisions by eligibility state and position and compare declare rates with the pre-2021 base rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Dispersion widens roughly linearly with consensus rank and is right-skewed for positions with a premium
nonlinearities.why: The standard deviation of realized pick around consensus is small for the top prospects and large later, so probabilities for top-5 and exact-slot events fall sharply with the rank, unlike over/under events near the middle.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic step: quarterback selection probability jumps once need exceeds a no-franchise-QB threshold
nonlinearities.why: A holder with a franchise QB almost never takes one in round one while a holder without one near the top does with high probability, so the response is a step, not a linear need effect.

nonlinearities.shape: Trade probability rises convexly with the consensus gap between the first and second prospects at a slot
nonlinearities.why: When one prospect is clearly above the rest, buyers pay to move; when prospects are equal, the pick holder keeps the slot, so trade risk is convex in the gap.
P(count >= N) collapses once N exceeds the number of realistic draftees, and the rounds 1-3 argmax pays 1/N on ties, so the payoff is a step function of small integer counts.

mechanism.summary: A Super Bowl MVP outcome factors into three layers. First, team layer: which two teams reach the game (conference path and seeding) and who wins at a neutral site after two weeks, using full-strength lineups. Second, game layer: given a win, the in-game script and box score decide which player posts a standout line (a passing line with multiple touchdowns, a large rushing or receiving game, several sacks, a defensive or return touchdown), which depends on who is available and the matchup. Third, voting layer: a media panel and a fan vote convert highlights into a name, with a quarterback premium, split credit among teammates and decisions made late in the game. Position and non-QB variants are aggregations of the same chain over player sets.

stages.name: Team path: which teams reach the Super Bowl
stages.description: Each conference champion emerges from a bracket after seeding, byes and matchups; the weeks before the final shift each team's chance to reach it. The set of finalists is uncertain in November and is a draw from a season simulation with playoff structure, not a ranking.
stages.distribution: Discrete finalist-pair distribution from simulation; heavy mass on top seeds

stages.name: Final: neutral-site winner at full strength
stages.description: The finalists play at a neutral site after a two-week gap, with no home advantage, a playoff overtime rule and lineups that change with injury returns and losses. The winner's identity is a close-to-coin-flip draw modified by the margin SD, so the favourite's win rate is modest even with a rating edge.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with win probability typically 35-65 percent; margin SD near 13 points

stages.name: Game script: who dominates the winner's game
stages.description: Conditional on the winner, the game shape (high scoring through the air, controlled run game, defensive turnovers, special-teams score) determines which unit posts the visible line; pace, pass rate and late-lead behavior matter, and overtime adds snaps.
stages.distribution: Mixture over script regimes with correlated player lines

stages.name: Player lines and credit allocation among the winner's players
stages.description: Given a script, the winner's players post lines: passing yards and TDs for a quarterback, yards and scores for receivers and backs, sacks and takeaways for defenders. Credit is shared when two teammates post strong lines, so top-line outliers drive the winner and teammate splits lower each player's probability.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed single-game lines; credit is a softmax over correlated candidates

stages.name: Voting and announcement
stages.description: A media panel and a fan vote name the MVP; fan voting closes during the fourth quarter, so ballots reflect the game state then, not the final whistle. Quarterbacks are favoured, narratives matter, and co-MVP or losing-team winners are rare. The position contract then maps the winner to strikes via the league depth chart at game time, with several strikes possible for one player.
stages.distribution: Categorical outcome with QB premium and rare exceptions; position markets are aggregations

stages.name: In-game state at ballot time (if markets trade live)
stages.description: If the contracts trade after kickoff, the information set is the live score, win probability and running player lines. Credit concentrates on the leading performer of the team ahead when ballots close in the fourth quarter; late plays after the fan-vote close move the panel only partly. Pre-game inputs then act only as priors for the remaining quarters.
stages.distribution: Time-varying categorical over candidates; collapses toward one player as the game state hardens; jump risk from late scores
